thread.title: Trump Authorizes CIA Operations in Venezuela
thread.title_full: Trump Authorizes CIA Operations in Venezuela

author: Emily Ross
title: Trump Authorizes CIA Operations in Venezuela
text:
The Trump administration has authorized the CIA to conduct covert operations in Venezuela, U.S. officials confirmed Wednesday.
President Trump said the move was part of a broader campaign to drive socialist leader Nicolás Maduro from power.
CIA Covert Operations
The authorization, known as a “presidential finding,” gives the CIA authority to conduct lethal operations in Venezuela and across the Caribbean.
Officials said the decision marks a major escalation in the administration’s pressure campaign against Maduro’s regime.
The authorization allows the CIA to act independently or alongside U.S. military operations.
It remains unclear if any missions have been launched under the new authority.
Speaking to reporters, President Trump confirmed he had approved the covert action.
“We are certainly looking at land now, because we’ve got the sea very well under control,” Trump said.
He was referring to recent U.S. strikes on boats off the Venezuelan coast, which killed 27 people accused of smuggling drugs.
The President said the ultimate goal is to end Maduro’s rule and stop Venezuela’s role in narcotics trafficking.
Ratcliffe and Rubio’s Strategy
The Venezuela strategy was developed by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, working with CIA Director John Ratcliffe.
Both men have described Maduro as a “narcoterrorist” who profits from the drug trade.
Rubio has called Maduro’s government “illegitimate” and vowed to support Venezuela’s democratic opposition.
Ratcliffe has promised to make the CIA “more aggressive” and willing to take risks under Trump’s orders.
The U.S. currently has around 10,000 troops stationed in the region, mostly in Puerto Rico.
American forces include Marines aboard amphibious ships and eight surface warships patrolling the Caribbean.
Officials said new strike options inside Venezuela are being prepared for Trump’s consideration.
Reward for Maduro’s Arrest
Trump recently ended diplomatic talks with Maduro after accusing him of sending violent criminals into the United States.
“Venezuela emptied their prisons into the United States of America,” Trump said Wednesday.
He cited the Tren de Aragua gang, which he has labeled a terrorist organization.
An intelligence assessment in February contradicted that claim, concluding the gang was not under Maduro’s control.
After the report was reaffirmed, Trump fired the acting head of the National Intelligence Council.
The U.S. has offered a $50 million reward for information leading to Maduro’s capture and conviction.
Washington has accused Maduro of leading a drug trafficking network and harboring terrorist groups.
CIA’s Role in Latin America
The CIA has long worked with Latin American governments on intelligence and counternarcotics missions.
But direct lethal operations by the agency in the region have been rare.
The new order signals a shift toward a more aggressive covert posture.
The CIA has a complicated history in Latin America, including coups and assassinations during the Cold War.
The agency orchestrated the 1954 coup in Guatemala and the failed 1961 Bay of Pigs invasion in Cuba.
It was also linked to coups in Brazil, Chile, and the Contra war in Nicaragua.
